Refunds are asynchronous, full or partial within 180 days, and take up to five minutes to complete as documented. Stripe sends refund.updated or refund.failed for the final result; the Refund becomes succeeded or failed, and failure returns the amount to Stripe balance with an alternative refund left to the merchant. Revolut decides disputes after evidence submission; Stripe notifies by email, Dashboard and charge.dispute.created if webhooks are configured, holds the amount until resolution, and returns it or makes the debit permanent based on the decision (old 122-145; new 122-146). Browser return alone establishes no payment status, capture or payout.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-revolut-pay-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-revolut-pay-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-revolut-pay.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/revolut-pay`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/revolut-pay, the November 7 overview describes a Revolut account holder paying from Revolut balance or a linked card. On mobile Stripe opens the app for authentication and confirmation, and desktop customers scan the QR with the app before returning to the site (new raw lines 7-11). The May overview describes website redirection and first-time checkout or saving by non-Revolut users (old raw lines 6-10). The same May overview and the November overview both say in their Disputes section that customers must authenticate by logging into their Revolut account (old raw lines 126-130; new raw lines 126-130). May's opening and disputes wording therefore leave the historical scope of guest checkout unresolved, and November's revised opening does not establish that the option was withdrawn. The two captures retain the linked Dashboard setup and product support, customer-initiated confirmation, one-time and recurring use, manual capture support, six currencies and the detailed business-country and customer scopes. The refund can succeed or fail asynchronously, with final webhook and failure restoring the amount to Stripe balance. Disputed funds are held pending Revolut's decision (old raw lines 122-154; new raw lines 122-155). source-stripe-revolut-pay.md captures the older behavior and stable features but should qualify the shopper scope and complete the refund and dispute boundaries. Return to the merchant is distinct from a verified successful payment.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/revolut-pay, November 7 substantively reframes the documented customer scope and adds explicit mobile-app versus desktop QR authentication to the overview (new raw lines 7-11; old raw lines 6-10). The separate May acceptance guide already describes both device paths and also has dated live-mode automatic-approval language that needs qualification. Preserve May's first-time and non-account saving claims as historical in source-stripe-revolut-pay.md. November's replacement demo URL and Elements quickstart link are navigation and presentation changes (old raw lines 98-120; new raw lines 99-120). Keep the explicit country table including Liechtenstein and Norway, default-currency and settlement/presentment wording in scope, and the stable refund and dispute deadlines, especially the 35 calendar days from evidence submission (old raw lines 122-154; new raw lines 122-155). Preserve wallet, Revolut Pay concept, acceptance, future-payment and separately dated subscription routes and reconcile reciprocal overview links.
